_comment: OpenDDE runtime on the SERVED path, recovered from the JapanFold platform's own job history (/home/cust-team/.aiand-bio/jobs/*/out/*results_*/results.json on GWH02) rather than from a bench (ws:japanfold-opendde-1024-uncap). runtime_s is tt_bio/worker.py:2047, the whole job inside the worker, so it includes the MSA search a bench fold skips by reading a precomputed alignment off disk. Only rows from today's engine (c2507852) are listed; the 779/788 rows in the same history are ~28 days old on a different engine and are not comparable. This is the number the catalog's runtime rule should be read against: a served 896 is 89% of the 1500 s predict watchdog, where the bench 1040 s reads as 69%.

note: real keyless job through https://api.japanfold.aiand.com/v1/predictions; CIF downloaded and scored with perf/ceilings/struct_signal.py off the box
same, opendde-abag checkpoint; distinct CIF md5 from the opendde job, so the two checkpoints are genuinely both exercised

_slope: 686 -> 896 on the served path is 3.97 s/residue, against 4.01 s/residue for the 896 -> 1024 bench pair, so the two paths differ by an additive ~300 s rather than by slope. The 1200 s / 80% margin line therefore falls near 865 aa on the served path (869 aa under a power-law fit, exponent 3.6), not the 936 aa the bench numbers gave. 896 still ships because measured_wall is the largest size measured to fold and OpenDDE carries no max_residues, so it refuses nothing.

_orphan_note: abag896new, a direct 896 aa opendde-abag leg on card 5, was killed by its own 2400 s timeout at rc=124 while the sibling opendde leg on the same card at the same size took 1039.6 s. Cause not isolated; the leg overlapped both served 896 jobs plus three orphaned spawn workers. It does not weaken the abag 896 claim, which rests on the served job above. NOTE: `timeout` killed the parent python and left the multiprocessing spawn worker running at 131% CPU holding the card -- the outer-pid kill does not reach the engine child.
